newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases 10 bps to 11.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases 10 bps to 11.7 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate eased 10 basis points to 11.7 percent on Monday despite a relatively high demand for fresh kuna funds.
Daily settlements totalled 48.5 million kuna, with demand for money overshooting supply by 12.1 million.
Fresh placements accounted for 36.5 million kuna and some 50 percent were interbank call money loans.
The weighted call money rate rose to 10.9 percent after some lenders raised their price to 11 from 10.5 percent earlier.
Term rates were not immediately affected, ending at between nine percent for insurers' one-week funds and a maximum 18 percent for one-month kuna granted by banks.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday firmer at 6.0999 against the dollar and 3.5703 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
